implementation: Added explicit cpu, auto, cuda, and cuda:N selection. auto selects the first GPU visible through the PyTorch CUDA-compatible API (CUDA or ROCm) and falls back to CPU; ambiguous plain cuda selection is rejected when multiple GPUs are visible.

Managed and manual training move supported nested mapping/list/tuple/namedtuple batch tensors to the selected device. External loops receive context.device and context.to_device(batch); custom objects are not guessed or mutated.
Runtime reports record requested/selected device, backend, device name, and measured memory. CPU reports process peak RSS; GPU reports allocated/reserved/peak/free/total memory where available.
Checkpoint resume validates selected device/backend identity and captures device RNG state. Repeated runs inherit device selection unless explicitly overridden.
OOM errors preserve training phase and report available measured resources with actionable structured diagnostics; no OOM prediction guarantee is claimed.

validation.result: passed: 8 tests, including explicit CPU and auto fallback, unavailable/ambiguous GPU rejection, actual ROCm single-GPU managed/manual/external execution, checkpoint save/resume, device drift rejection and injected OOM reporting.
passed: 13 tests across data preset training, managed/manual/external modes, checkpoint device RNG and resume integrity.
passed: 66 worker modules, complete embedded asset coverage, imports follow domain direction.
passed: Rust/Python protocol, API, state formats and required features match.

hardware_evidence: See docs/device-support.json. Verified on Linux x86_64 with AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT / ROCm; one local profile only.
integration_patch: CLI --device is persisted with training inputs and inherited on repeat/resume; explicitly changing the device for a checkpoint resume is rejected.
Device runtime module is included in embedded worker assets and protocol compatibility checks pass.
Product documentation advertises only the tested single-GPU profile and leaves CUDA/NVIDIA unverified.
remaining: No NVIDIA CUDA hardware was available; NVIDIA support remains unverified.
OOM handling used an injected OOM exception; no physical memory-exhaustion stress test was performed.
No distributed or multi-GPU training is implemented in this task.
